The main takeaway from our work is that
foraminiferal analyses can be used as an effective paleoenvironmental proxy in the absence of other proxies such as corals, mollusks, and bryozoans.

foraminiferal analysis of shelf-edge slope sediments can be used to infer paleoenvironmental conditions, and that the resulting data can be used to reconstruct sea-level changes and their effects on the GBR shelf slopes.
the GBR slope sediments are a record of the past reef growth and sea-level fluctuations, and thus provide a valuable archive for understanding how coral reefs respond to past sea-level changes.
